title: Long, et al. v. James River Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC denied the complaint. On the parties' sole stipulated issue, it answered 'No' to whether JRP erred by instructing TE Andrew Conrad not to teach or preach his views on creation and anthropomorphic days, leaving the instruction in effect. The adopted decision was approved 13 concurring, 8 dissenting, 1 recused, and 2 absent.
first_summary: James River Presbytery instructed a newly ordained teaching elder not to teach or preach his views on creation and anthropomorphic days. The SJC denied the complaint, holding the complainants failed to prove procedural or constitutional error and that deference was owed to the presbytery. The dissent argued the presbytery exceeded its discretion by restricting views on creation that the PCA has historically allowed.
summary: At issue was whether James River Presbytery erred by instructing TE Andrew Conrad not to teach or preach his views that the Genesis days were not necessarily six twenty-four-hour days, after JRP treated the views as an exception. The SJC denied the complaint, leaving JRP's instruction in effect. It deferred under BCO 39-3, finding no significant procedural or constitutional error and no clear error of discretion; the parties had stipulated that instruction as the sole issue. The eight dissenters would have found JRP exceeded its discretion.

Line 41 states the parties stipulated the sole issue: whether JRP erred in giving that instruction.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 47-49 give the judgment 'No.' Lines 53-71 give the adopted reasoning: no errors of process or unconstitutional acts, no proof of clear error of discretion or judgment, and deference to the lower court under BCO 39-3. Line 73 records the split vote.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 75-112 are a dissenting opinion, not the adopted ruling. Its liberty-of-conscience, historical creation-freedom, and prior-GA arguments are dissent positions; the majority did not adopt them. Lines 114-122 concern unrelated other-case dispositions and are not part of this case.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No incorporated decision supplies a material result for this case. The dissent cites prior decisions such as Case 95-7, Bowen, and Case 97-5, but they are referenced only in dissent and are not adopted in the SJC judgment.
